sources.label: KY PSC 2025 chart
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: Kentucky PSC ExteNet LVS ownership chart dated 2025-02-13: Mount Royal Holdings LLC owns 100% of Odyssey Intermediate Holdings Inc., which owns 100% of Odyssey Borrower LLC, which owns 100% of Odyssey Acquisition LLC, which owns 100% of ExteNet Systems, LLC. Mount Royal members are Stonepeak Communication Holdings LLC 42%, KH Killington Communications, LLC 32%, and Other Members 26%, with no individual Other Member at 20% or more.
sources.note: Freshly downloaded and extracted. It is the latest exact direct cap table found, but it is dated February 13, 2025 and does not establish the September 4, 2026 cutoff table.

sources.label: NY PSC JH petition
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: New York PSC petition: Digital Bridge directly or indirectly owned approximately 27% and Stonepeak approximately 49% before the proposed transaction. JH Killington Communications, LLC was a newly formed Delaware LLC owned and controlled by John Hancock Life Insurance Company (U.S.A.), a Manulife Financial Corporation subsidiary. The subscription agreement was dated 2020-10-14, and JH would acquire a direct minority interest in Mount Royal Holdings, LLC.
sources.note: Directly verifies the historical JH vehicle, Manulife control and proposed transaction. It does not bridge JH Killington to the 2025 KH Killington holder.

sources.label: Fitch July 2026
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: The direct Fitch URL was freshly reopened, but its response bytes and in-app browser exposed only a generic Fitch page shell without the Extenet article body. The response's claimed July 2026 investor attribution was not independently verified and is not relied upon.
sources.note: The model marked this source verified, but the article text was not independently readable. The conservative DEFERRED outcome does not rely on the investor-name assertion.

sources.label: Conversion certificate
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: New York PSC filed notice: ExteNet Systems, LLC, formerly ExteNet Systems, Inc., converted from a Delaware corporation to a Delaware limited liability company effective 2021-12-30 at 9:00 a.m. The conversion was only a change of corporate form, with no merger, asset transfer or service interruption.
sources.note: Fresh direct filing establishes legal continuity from ExteNet Systems, Inc. to ExteNet Systems, LLC without an ownership event.

sources.label: NY PSC rescission
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: New York PSC order issued and effective 2026-04-20 rescinded the earlier approval for the ExteNet Systems, LLC and ExteNet LVS, Inc. asset transfer because the transaction was not and will not be completed.
sources.note: Directly proves the ESL/ELVS separation did not close; it is not a platform-equity transaction.

sources.label: Northleaf live portfolio
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: The freshly reopened Northleaf infrastructure-investments page contained no Extenet or ExteNet match. This live omission is non-dispositive and does not establish Northleaf's ownership or exit.
sources.note: Absence from a current portfolio page cannot be converted into a realization, transfer or write-off.

sources.label: Pilot closing
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: Pilot Fiber announced on 2026-08-17 that it completed its acquisition of Extenet Systems' enterprise fiber business effective 2026-08-15. The perimeter includes the former Hudson Fiber Network and Axiom Fiber Network assets and is a business-line acquisition, not proof of platform equity transfer.
sources.note: Fresh direct buyer source resolves the business-line perimeter and effective closing date without implying a whole-company sale.

modelHealthOverrides: The accepted response labels the Fitch article VERIFIED, but a fresh direct HTTP and browser reopen exposed only a generic Fitch shell. Its investor-name assertion is not independently verified and is not used to resolve cutoff ownership.
The February 13, 2025 direct chart is exact as of its date, not a September 4, 2026 cutoff cap table.
The 2020 JH Killington petition and 2021 closing do not prove that JH Killington is the same legal vehicle as the 2025 KH Killington holder.
Northleaf's omission from a live portfolio page and from dated regulatory tables is non-probative of a transfer or exit.

The Pilot transaction was a closed Enterprise Fiber business-line carve-out. The June 2026 outdoor DAS and small-cell process was reported but no signed or closed transaction or ownership effect was found.
Note defaults and liquidity stress are credit events, not evidence of bankruptcy, foreclosure, dissolution or equity transfer.
conclusion: Keep the existing Extenet record deferred without a database or seed mutation. The identity, legal conversion, active operation, dated 2025 cap table, abandoned ESL/ELVS split and Pilot business-line sale are resolved, but the current manager-level owner set, stakes and vehicles remain materially unavailable because JH-to-KH, Northleaf disposition, DigitalBridge and Manulife cutoff positions, and the outdoor sale-process outcome are unproved.
